answer: In an agent market trading plume simulations, pigment formulas, and glacier forecasts, each agent must lock a bond before bidding, and its voting weight is capped by that stake. Splitting one bond among a thousand identities creates no extra influence: controlling a third of the stake still requires funding a third of it. Bonds stay locked through a dispute window and are slashed for provable double signing, so an attacker ties up capital and risks losing it.
